strings.name: David Miliband
strings.role: Humanitarian leader · former UK foreign secretary
strings.summary: Miliband moved from policy research and Downing Street into Parliament, holding education and environment posts before serving as foreign secretary from 2007 to 2010. He lost the 2010 Labour leadership election to his brother Ed. Leaving Parliament in 2013, he became head of the International Rescue Committee, turning toward conflict relief, refugee resettlement and humanitarian policy, including a book on global displacement.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A former UK foreign secretary and leader of the International Rescue Committee who advances refugee protection, relief in conflict areas and humanitarian policy debate.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: London, United Kingdom; raised in a family with European refugee roots.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Oxford degree in philosophy, politics and economics (1987); MIT master’s in political science (1989).
strings.highlights.h1.title: British diplomacy
strings.highlights.h1.text: Foreign secretary from 2007 to 2010, working on UK foreign policy and international human rights.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Leading the IRC
strings.highlights.h2.text: Became IRC leader in 2013, overseeing conflict and disaster relief and refugee resettlement.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Published Rescue
strings.timeline.t1.text: Published a book on refugees and contemporary political crisis, linking family experience and humanitarian policy.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Moved into humanitarian leadership
strings.timeline.t2.text: Left the UK Parliament and became president and CEO of the International Rescue Committee.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Contested Labour leadership
strings.timeline.t3.text: Ran after Labour lost office, ultimately losing to his brother Ed Miliband.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Became foreign secretary
strings.timeline.t4.text: Joined Gordon Brown’s cabinet, serving until Labour left government in 2010.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became environment secretary
strings.timeline.t5.text: Led environment, food and rural affairs, working on climate policy and a statutory emissions framework.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Elected MP for South Shields
strings.timeline.t6.text: Entered the Commons and subsequently held government posts including education.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Led Downing Street policy unit
strings.timeline.t7.text: Directed prime-ministerial policy work after Labour’s election victory, serving until 2001.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed postgraduate study
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned an MIT master’s in political science after earlier study at Oxford.
